diagnosis: All three seeds fail identically and deterministically, with every primitive reporting [ok] and FAILURES: 0 — so the failure is geometric, not a crash, IK miss, or perception miss. Arm0 grasps the hammer at the point get_hammer_pose() returns (the middle of the handle), lifts, carries and reorients it so the handle runs along +X; keyframes seed0_step004 and seed0_step007 confirm those stages all work. Because arm0 never regrasps, the held point is still the handle middle, so when arm0 presents the hammer with its gripper at the hardcoded x = handover_x - 0.10 = 0.71, the free handle only extends to roughly x = 0.80 (about 0.09 m of exposed shaft, measured by scaling the hammer in seed0_step009 against the two known gripper x-positions). The baseline nonetheless sends arm1 to the hardcoded absolute coordinate handover_x + 0.05 = 0.86, roughly 6 cm past the handle tip: arm1 closes on air at step 010, arm0 opens at step 011, and the hammer drops to the floor (seed{0,1,2}_step011/012 show it on the floor with both of arm1's fingers shut on nothing). The root cause is that arm1's grasp target is a hardcoded world coordinate encoding an assumption about where the handle tip would end up, rather than a point derived from the hammer's observed pose — the two are unrelated, so the reach overshoots the object. The proposed repair re-perceives the hammer via get_hammer_pose() after arm0 has lifted and reoriented it, and derives arm1's grasp as a short offset along the exposed handle from that observed pose, removing the dead reckoning. IMPORTANT: outcome is 'fail', not 'success', for two reasons documented in BLOCKED.md — (1) no replay harness is reachable (Bash is sandboxed to the task directory, which contains no runner), so 0 of the 3 permitted replay attempts per seed could be spent and fix_code.py is reasoned-but-never-executed; and (2) task.md is a placeholder with no runtime task language, so the success predicate — including the baseline's asserted handover z-band [0.15, 0.20] and '>8cm gripper buffer' — is unconfirmed. The fix's HANDLE_GRASP_OFFSET = 0.06 lands on the shaft but leaves the grippers only ~6 cm apart, which violates that asserted buffer; honouring it would require arm0 to grasp off-centre toward the head, which needs a head-direction inference I cannot verify without a replay and did not risk.

proposed_skills.name: anchor-second-grasp-to-reperceived-object-pose
proposed_skills.failure_signature: Every primitive returns [ok] with no IK or perception failure, but the object is dropped or missed at a late handover/insertion stage. The second grasp's target is a hardcoded world coordinate or an offset dead-reckoned from a pre-transport pose, and the gripper closes on air near — but not on — the object.
proposed_skills.when_to_apply: Any multi-stage task where one arm (or one stage) transports an object and a later stage must grasp or engage that same object at a point whose world position depends on where the transport actually ended up: bimanual handovers, regrasp/reorient sequences, place-into-fixture, tool handoffs. Especially when the transported object is held off its centroid, so the target feature's position is the held point plus an object-geometry offset rather than the commanded pose.
proposed_skills.strategy: Never let the second grasp target an absolute coordinate. After the transporting arm reaches its presentation pose, call the perception primitive AGAIN to read the object's actual current pose, then compute the second grasp as that observed pose plus a short offset along the exposed feature. This closes the loop over grasp slip, carry error and the offset between the commanded gripper pose and the object's held point — all of which silently accumulate under dead reckoning. Choose the offset to stay inside the exposed span (measure the span from keyframes if the geometry is unknown); if the span is too short to also clear the two grippers, that is a signal the transporting arm must grasp off-centre earlier, not that the offset should be stretched. Re-perceiving also cheaply verifies the first grasp held.
proposed_skills.code_sketch:
# BAD: absolute coordinate, unrelated to where the object actually is
# arm1_grasp_pos = np.array([handover_x + 0.05, 0.0, handover_z])

# GOOD: present, then re-perceive, then offset along the exposed feature
goto_pose_arm0(present_pos, carry_quat)
obj_pos, obj_quat = get_object_pose()   # actual pose after transport
arm1_grasp_pos = np.array([
    obj_pos[0] + EXPOSED_FEATURE_OFFSET,  # inside the exposed span
    obj_pos[1],
    obj_pos[2],
])
open_gripper_arm1()
goto_pose_arm1(arm1_grasp_pos, arm1_grasp_quat, z_approach=0.12)
close_gripper_arm1()

proposed_skills.name: held-point-offset-bounds-bimanual-separation
proposed_skills.failure_signature: A bimanual handover is planned with a fixed gripper-separation buffer, but the second gripper either closes on air (reaching past the object) or the two grippers collide. The transporting arm holds the object at its centroid or at whatever point the perception primitive reports.
proposed_skills.when_to_apply: Planning any handover or dual-contact manipulation where both grippers must be on the object simultaneously, and the first arm's grasp point was chosen by perception (e.g. an object-pose call returning a centre) rather than deliberately placed.
proposed_skills.strategy: Treat the exposed span — from the first arm's held point to the far end of the graspable feature — as a hard budget that bounds the achievable gripper separation. If the required buffer exceeds that span, no choice of second-grasp offset can satisfy both constraints, and the fix belongs at the FIRST grasp: offset it toward the far end of the object so more of the feature is exposed. Derive the exposed span from keyframes before committing to a separation buffer, and check the buffer against it at plan time rather than discovering the conflict as an air grasp. Note the ordering risk: moving the first grasp off-centre requires knowing the object's asymmetry direction in the world frame, so establish that by replay before relying on it — a sign error converts a late, well-diagnosed failure into an early one.
proposed_skills.code_sketch:
# Budget check at plan time, before committing to the second grasp.
EXPOSED_SPAN = 0.09        # held point -> far end, measured from keyframes
REQUIRED_BUFFER = 0.08     # desired gripper separation

if REQUIRED_BUFFER > EXPOSED_SPAN - GRASP_MARGIN:
    # Infeasible from a centred grasp: expose more feature at grasp time
    # by offsetting the FIRST grasp toward the far end of the object.
    grasp_pos = obj_pos + AWAY_FROM_FEATURE * FIRST_GRASP_OFFSET
else:
    grasp_pos = obj_pos
